newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dec JGB up sharply by noon on BOJ's rate comment.
newsitem.headline: Dec JGB up sharply by noon on BOJ's rate comment.

text.p: The key December Japanese Government Bond (JGB) contract was up sharply by Tokyo midday on Monday due to dealers' short covering sparked by a remark by Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita acknowledging recent falls in long-term yields, traders said.

"Long-term interest rates have previously reflected expectations of stronger economic prospects but some changes have been seen recently, in accordance with conditions." Matsushita said in Washington, where he attended the annual meetings of World Bank and International Monetary Fund.
December was at 121.90 at noon, up from Friday's 121.45.
In the cash market, persistent, though small-lot, buying of long-term JGBs by institutional investors was detected.
Traders said investors had been interested in buying-on-dips lately, but wary of more purchases on the price recovery, as JGB prices have already hit record-high levels.
"However, comments like this morning (by Matsushita) made it comfortable for them to buy on the recovery as well," said a brokerage trader.
The yield of the benchmark 182nd JGB was at 2.845 percent at 0230 GMT, down from 2.870 percent on Friday.
On Friday, JGBs tumbled on a media report which quoted a senior Bank of Japan official as saying that the central bank was concerned about any excessive decline in long-term yields.
Matsushita's comment on Monday effectively denied the context of the media report by acknowledging the recent falls in the yields, traders said.
The market was awaiting August industrial output data due at 0630 GMT. A Reuters poll of economists produced an average forecast of a 1.5 percent month-on-month fall.
